expert.visuals_analysis:
[PLOT: roc_curve]
The ROC curve is a plot of sensitivity (true positive rate) against 1-specificity (false positive rate). A higher area under the curve (AUC) indicates better model performance. The curve here shows an AUC of 97%, indicating strong discriminative power.

[PLOT: pr_curve]
The precision-recall curve plots precision (positive predictive value) against recall (sensitivity). High values in both dimensions indicate a well-performing model, especially useful when dealing with imbalanced datasets.

[PLOT: confusion_matrix]
The confusion matrix is a table that shows the number of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives. A perfect matrix would have no off-diagonal elements, indicating no misclassifications.

[PLOT: corr_heatmap]
The correlation heatmap visualizes the pairwise correlation between features. Colors range from blue (negative correlation) to red (positive correlation). The heatmap here shows a moderate positive correlation between mean radius and mean texture.

[PLOT: feature_importance]
The feature importance plot ranks features based on their contribution to model predictions. Higher values indicate more important features. Here, 'mean radius' is the most important feature with an importance score of 0.45.

[PLOT: shap_summary]
The SHAP summary plot shows the impact of each feature on model predictions. Positive values indicate that increasing the feature value increases the likelihood of a positive prediction (malignancy), while negative values have the opposite effect.
